newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises in winter as trade moves further oUT.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises in winter as trade moves further oUT.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw a larger volume of trade than in recent days on Thursday, with most prices firming up, and with a huge range of periods traded, dealers said.

There was a large volume of within-day trade done, and the same player who was involved in purchasing most of this was also involved in two deals for the gas year starting in October 1998 and finishing in September 1999. So the period spanned by the deals done is nearly two and a half years, and many individual quarters in between - especially this coming winter - were also covered.

The bulk of activity was centred on this winter, with prices rising significantly over the day. A trade was done at 15.90 pence in the morning before climbing to 16.05 where at least one trade was done.

One dealer reported a bid/offer spread of 16.00/16.075 in late afternoon, but brokers said it then slipped back slightly to the range 15.95/16.05 pence. This compares with a closing assessment on Wednesday of 15.80/15.95 pence a therm.

There was also good interest seen for the fourth quarter this year, with prices also ticking up, but the biggest rises were seen in Q1. A trader whose company did several deals in both Q4 and Q1 was surprised by the increase in volume.
"It's either shortcovering or genuine demand shorts that are driving the market today," he said, although he said it seemed surprising that people would need to cover short positions so far forward.

There were rumours that gas for the year from this October had traded at 12.65 pence and 12.80 pence, although this was not confirmed. And a trader who had been involved in the trades for the October 1998 gas year said he believed a 1997/1998 gas year spread had been done at a differential of 0.90 pence a therm, with the 1998 year stronger.

Another dealer said the reason for the strength of the 1998 year over 1997 was that the Interconnector pipeline, providing an outlet for UK gas on to mainland Europe, will be open by the start of the 1998 gas year and is expected to boost prices.

On the IPE futures market trade was disappointingly quiet, with only 95 lots done in five separate trades. Most of the activity was done in the back months and at higher prices, in line with the trend on the physical market.
